entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: ?Court No. - 74

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 17217 of 2023
Applicant :- Nasibuddin

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Priyavrat Tripathi,Ravi Chandra Srivastava
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Heard Sri Priyavrat Tripathi, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Ravi Kant Kushwaha,
learned Aga for the State-respondent.

2.  The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
147 of 2020, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station- Sadar Bazar, District- Saharanpur, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged against applicant and his nine relatives and according to the FIR, marriage of the sister of the informant was performed with the applicant on 16.9.2016 and after marriage, applicant and his family members used to torture the sister of the informant for want of Rs. 2.5 lacs and a motor-cycle and on 13.2.2020 the sister of the informant informed on phone to the informant that his in-laws ablazed her for want of dowry and when informant arrived at Saharanpur then he came to know that in-laws of his sister has taken her to PGI, Chandigarh and when he arrived at Chandigarh then found that his sister was burned and on 21.2.2020 his sister again informed him that applicant and his family members ablazed her and it is further mentioned in the FIR that during treatment on 22.2.2020 sister of the informant i.e. wife of the applicant died due to her burn injuries.

Nasibuddin vs State Of U.P. on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64298380/
1 4.
Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is the husband of the deceased and he has falsely been implicated by the informant in the present matter.
He further submitted that applicant neither demanded any dowry nor he and his family members ever tortured the deceased in any manner.

He further submitted that incident is said to have been taken place on 13.2.2020 and deceased died on 22.2.2020 but in spite of that FIR of the present case was lodged on 1.3.2020 i.e.
after about more than two weeks from the date of incident and after about more than a week from the date of death of the deceased.
5.
He further submitted that this inordinate delay in lodging the FIR itself casts serious doubt on the prosecution case.

He further submitted that actually wife of the applicant accidentally caught fire while she was cooking food on stove and at that time applicant was not at home and after receiving information, he immediately arrived at home and rushed to the hospital along with his wife and his wife was admitted by him in the District Hospital, Saharanpur and this fact is evident from Annexure No.- 2.
6.

He further submitted that from the District Hospital, Saharanpur deceased was referred to PGI,
Chandigarh and thereafter applicant and his family members took her to PGI, Chandigarh and this fact is itself admitted by the informant in the FIR as well in his statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. and in spite of the best effort of the doctors deceased died on 22.2.2020.

7. He further submitted that deceased was not in a position to give any statement and this fact is evident from a G.D. entry dated 18.2.2020 which has been annexed as Annexure No. 3 to the affidavit and this fact completely belies the story narrated by the informant that on 21.2.2020 in the hospital his sister i.e. deceased informed him that applicant and his family members ablazed her.
He further submitted that no reliance can be placed on the version of the FIR that on 13.2.2020 immediately after the incident deceased informed that her in-laws ablazed her.

8. He further submitted that immediately after the incident, applicant admitted the deceased in the hospital but in spite of the best medical treatment, deceased died and this fact shows the bona-fide on the part of the applicant and in the present matter, applicant is in jail since 26.6.2020 i.e. for last about more than two and half years and trial of the case till date could not be concluded

, therefore,
applicant may be released on bail.

9. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that applicant is the husband and his wife died due to burn injury within 7 years of her marriage and there is also allegation of dowry but learned AGA could not dispute the fact that from the perusal of the record, it appears that immediately after the incident, applicant admitted the deceased in the District Hospital, Saharanpur and thereafter he took her to PGI, Chandigarh where she expired and in the present matter, he is in jail since June, 2020 i.e. for last about more than two and half years.
10. I have counsels for both the parties and perused the record of the case.

11. Although, applicant is the husband and his wife i.e. deceased died due to burn injury within 7 years of her marriage and there was also allegation of demand of dowry against the applicant and his Nasibuddin vs State Of U.P. on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64298380/
2 family members and it is also mentioned in the FIR and in the statement of the informant recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. that immediately after the incident deceased informed him that applicant and his family members ablazed her and in the hospital she also informed him about this fact but record shows that applicant, the husband of the deceased, after incident immediately rushed to the district hospital along with the deceased and this fact is evident from Annexure No. 2 to the affidavit and thereafter he admitted her in PGI, Chandigarh and this fact has been admitted by the informant himself in the FIR as well as in his statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. therefore, this fact shows bona-fide of the applicant.

12. Further during investigation, some neighbours and nearby shopkeepers filed their respective affidavits and during investigation IO also recorded statement of one Ramjanam, who stated that at the time of incident, applicant was not at home and after receiving information, he rushed to his home and this fact clearly suggests that at the time of alleged incident of burning applicant was not at the home.
Further, applicant is in jail, in the present matter, since 26.6.2020 i.e. for last about more than two and half years and till date trial of the case could not be concluded.
13. Therefore, from the discussion made above, in my view applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
14. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

15. Let the applicant- Nasibuddin be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
16. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

Order Date :- 18.4.2023 KK Patel  Nasibuddin vs State Of U.P. on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64298380/
